title: The 8 Levels of Student Loans
house: A bustling metropolitan university city named Fructopolis, made of endless neon-lit campus libraries, cramped student apartments, and towering banking skyscrapers where giant fruit and vegetable people rush to their futures.
catchphrase: The number on your forehead never lies.
links: The barista in Level 2 mentions a tired strawberry student borrowing her textbook.
The library printer from Level 4 is seen smoking and jammed in the background of Level 6.
The mysterious sports car from Level 8 nearly splashes the broccoli student in Level 1.

levels.open_loop: Why did the financial aid office suddenly freeze her entire account right before final exams?

gegenspieler.tat: Laughs loudly at her rejected loan application in the crowded cafeteria and tells her to drop out.

levels.name: Ben, 20, Broccoli Student
levels.story: Minus 45.000 Dollar Schulden, kein Cent mehr auf dem Konto und der Dean droht mir live im Hörsaal mit dem Rauswurf. The 8 levels of student loans. Level 1. I am Ben, twenty, broccoli student, staring at my laptop screen in a freezing campus library while my stomach growls. I thought my part-time job at the diner would cover rent and instant ramen. Then the tuition fee hit harder than a freight train. You really think a veggie with that pathetic negative number will graduate? I swallow hard, my small green florets trembling with humiliation. But I know something he does not about this university's hidden grant fund. Then the dean walked in and said these exact words to me. Das siehst du in Level 2. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Mia, 21, Strawberry Barista
levels.story: Minus 28.000 Dollar und drei zerknüllte Dollarscheine im Trinkgelaglas – während die Chefin mich vor allen Kunden als Versagerin abstempelt. The 8 levels of student loans. Level 2. I am Mia, twenty-one, strawberry barista, rushing to steam oat milk while my phone buzzes with another text from the loan shark collection agency. My tiny studio apartment costs twelve hundred a month, and my textbook costs more than my entire kitchen setup. You probably cannot even afford a real espresso machine. I bite my tongue, wiping the counter with a shaking hand because I need this job to pay my interest rate. But then an old regular walked up and whispered something unbelievable. Das siehst du in Level 3. You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Leo, 22, Orange Engineering Major
levels.story: Minus 12.000 Dollar und mein Kollege klaut einfach meine komplette Abschlussarbeit vor den Augen des Prüfungsausschusses. The 8 levels of student loans. Level 3. I am Leo, twenty-two, orange engineering major, standing in the university workshop surrounded by copper wires and soldering irons. I built this entire solar-powered prototype with my bare hands. This thesis is mine now, old friend, your negative balance means the board will never fund your patent anyway. My citrus skin heats up with pure rage and helplessness. I spent four years surviving on instant oatmeal for this exact moment. But right as security grabbed my arm, the department head shouted these words. Das siehst du in Level 4. You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Maya, 23, Avocado Grad Student
levels.story: Exakt null Dollar auf dem Konto, und mein Vermieter wirft meine Abschlussarbeit auf den nassen Flur, weil ich mir die Miete nicht mehr leisten kann. The 8 levels of student loans. Level 4. I am Maya, twenty-three, avocado grad student, packing my entire life into cardboard boxes in a noisy student sublet. I paid off my first loan tier, but my landlord just doubled the rent because of neighborhood gentrification. Move your junk out of the way, my negative balance is already stressing me out enough without your cardboard castle. I roll my eyes, hugging my thesis notes to my chest like a shield. Nobody warned me that hitting zero would feel this terrifying. But then my phone rang with an unknown caller ID, and the voice on the other end said this. Das siehst du in Level 5. You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.name: Zoe, 24, Coconut Law Student
levels.story: Plus 18.500 Dollar Ersparnis, aber der Senior Partner zerreißt meine Bewerbung vor dem gesamten Büro und nennt mich eine arme Kirchenmaus. The 8 levels of student loans. Level 5. I am Zoe, twenty-four, coconut law student, clutching my internship application files outside the partner's oak double doors. I worked three graveyard shifts a week at the campus legal aid clinic just to afford these filing fees. Cute application, little nut, but pro bono work is charity for people who cannot do real corporate law. My hard fibrous shell aches with pure indignation after everything I sacrificed. Before I could fish my papers out of the bin, the senior partner turned around and whispered this. Das siehst du in Level 6. You'll see that in Level 6.

levels.name: Victor, 25, Dragon Fruit MBA
levels.story: Plus 85.000 Dollar, doch plötzlich steht mein alter Kommilitone im Auditorium und beschuldigt mich des Betrugs vor Investoren. The 8 levels of student loans. Level 6. I am Victor, twenty-five, dragon fruit MBA student, striding through the grand marble auditorium with my sleek tablet. I played the university game better than anyone, cutting costs and securing sponsorships. You rigged the innovation grant committee to steal my lab funding. I adjust my designer lapel and flash a cold smile. Welcome to real business, kid, ideas don't pay tuition, results do, I snap, stepping right past him toward the stage. I thought my financial victory was absolute. But then the university auditor stood up at the back of the room and announced this. Das siehst du in Level 7. You'll see that in Level 7.

levels.name: Marcus, 35, Coconut Tycoon
levels.story: Plus 210.000 Dollar und ich besitze inzwischen die Schuldenverträge von jedem Einzelnen, der mich damals gedemütigt hat. The 8 levels of student loans. Level 8. I am Marcus, thirty-five, coconut tycoon, standing on the penthouse balcony overlooking the illuminated Fructopolis skyline. Years ago, I started with a negative balance worse than any student on these streets, surviving on library coffee and borrowed textbooks. A young coconut law student tries to hand me an appeal file, but I simply look at her forehead and smile because I remember being her. We all played the exact same game of survival, climbing from negative numbers straight to the top of the financial empire. The number on our foreheads only shows where we started, not who we became in the end. Do you want to know which character in this city secretly bought your very first student loan contract?
